question.q: Is Oracle Streams still an option for replicating to Azure?
question.expected: No: desupported in Oracle Database 19c (deprecated since 12.1); name the replacement route (GoldenGate or a log-based CDC tool / Azure DMS where applicable).

result:
**Verdict: No.** Oracle Streams is deprecated and desupported by Oracle itself — it isn't a supported replication mechanism for any current Oracle release, and Azure has no service that reproduces it directly.

**Lifecycle status**
- Introduced pre-11.2; **deprecated in Oracle 12.1** and **desupported starting 19c** (19.1, per an April 2019 notice). Oracle's replacement is **GoldenGate**. — [Deprecated and Desupported Features for Oracle Database 12c (12.1)](https://docs.oracle.com/database/121/UPGRD/deprecated.htm), [Oracle Database Changes, Desupports, and Deprecations (Upgrade Guide 19c)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/upgrd/oracle-database-changes-deprecations-desupports.html)
- Streams never supported 12c-era multitenant features; note that **Advanced Queuing itself is not deprecated** and remains fully supported (Streams used AQ queues internally). — same 19c source above, per the feature summary in the dataset.

**Azure replication options mapped for Streams-era workloads (Oracle 11.2–18c scope in the dataset)**

| Azure target | Fidelity | Key caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Azure Database Migration Service | **none** | No online/continuous-sync scenario with Oracle as a source at all — only offline SSMA migrations to Azure SQL targets. [Azure Database Migration Service: supported migration scenarios](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dms/resource-scenario-status) |
| Azure Data Factory | **workaround** (effort L) | No native CDC or auto-incremental support for Oracle; requires a customer-managed watermark pipeline — batch micro-batches, not log-based streaming, and no delete capture without a soft-delete column. [Change data capture in Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/concepts-change-data-capture), [Copy data to and from Oracle with Azure Data Factory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-oracle) |
| Microsoft Fabric (mirroring) | **partial** (effort M) | Reads redo via LogMiner into OneLake Delta tables (latency as low as tens of seconds) but is one-directional into OneLake only, requires archive log mode, supplemental logging, and an on-premises data gateway — not database-to-database replication. [Mirror Oracle databases in Microsoft Fabric](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/mirroring/oracle) |
| Oracle Database@Azure | **partial** (effort M) | The Oracle-native successor, GoldenGate, is supported as a monitored deployment type for active-active replication, but is **not included** in the Database@Azure price and needs its own license; capture/replicat setup differs from Streams rules. [Business continuity and disaster recovery for Oracle Database@Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/oracle-on-azure/oracle-disaster-recovery-oracle-database-azure), [Overview: Oracle Database@Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/oracle/oracle-db/database-overview) |

All four mappings apply to Oracle versions **11.2, 12.1, 12.2, 18c**. Given Streams' 19c desupport, if you're planning on 19c or later, Streams isn't in scope at all and **GoldenGate on Oracle Database@Azure** is the closest documented replacement in this dataset.

**Disputes:** none recorded for Oracle Streams in the dataset.

**Gap:** the dataset has no mapping evaluating GoldenGate itself as an Azure-independent replication engine beyond the Oracle Database@Azure caveat above (e.g., GoldenGate on Oracle-on-Azure-VM targets isn't covered by a distinct mapping here).
